title: A and An: Talking About One Thing
summary: Use a and an before a singular countable noun when introducing one person or thing. Choose the article by the next spoken sound, and use these forms when describing people and their jobs.
learningObjectives: Choose a or an before an ordinary singular countable noun.
Choose the correct article before vowel and consonant sounds, including hour and university.
Describe what someone is or does using an appropriate article.
Use another to request one more item.

explanation.heading: A and an introduce one person or thing
explanation.body: Use a or an with a singular countable noun when you mention one item or person without identifying a particular one. Do not normally leave out the article before this kind of noun. Plural nouns and uncountable nouns do not take a/an in the same way.
explanation.example: There is a bicycle outside the café.

explanation.heading: Listen to the next sound, not only the first letter
explanation.body: Use an before a vowel sound and a before a consonant sound. The following word may be an adjective: choose the article by the first sound after it. We say an hour because the h is silent, but a university because university begins with a consonant /y/ sound.
explanation.example: It was an exciting evening at a university event.

explanation.heading: Say what a person or thing is
explanation.body: Use a/an when you identify a person or thing by a group, kind, or description. A singular job title usually needs a/an after be and similar expressions such as work as. The same pattern works with descriptions such as a small village or an unusual idea.

explanation.heading: Another means one more or a different one
explanation.body: Another is one word, built from an and other. Use another before a singular countable noun to ask for one additional item or a different item of that kind. Do not write an other as two words in this use.
explanation.example: Could we have another chair, please?

left.label: Vowel sound
left.note: Hour begins with a vowel sound because its h is silent.

right.label: Consonant sound
right.note: University begins with a /y/ sound, so use a.

comparisons.title: An item and one more item

examples.sentence: There is an orange in the fruit bowl.
examples.note: An goes before the vowel sound in orange.

examples.sentence: Theo bought a new jacket yesterday.
examples.note: A comes before the consonant sound in new.

examples.sentence: My neighbour works as a nurse.
examples.note: A singular profession normally takes a/an.

examples.sentence: They moved to a European city last year.
examples.note: European starts with a consonant /y/ sound.

examples.sentence: Can I have another biscuit with my tea?

commonMistakes.why: A singular job title normally needs an article.

commonMistakes.incorrect: I waited a hour for the train.
commonMistakes.correct: I waited an hour for the train.
commonMistakes.why: The h in hour is silent, so the next sound is a vowel.

commonMistakes.incorrect: She wears an uniform at work.
commonMistakes.correct: She wears a uniform at work.
commonMistakes.why: Uniform begins with a consonant /y/ sound.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Please bring me an other cup.
commonMistakes.why: Another is written as one word.

studyTips: Say the noun and any adjective aloud before deciding between a and an.
Remember that singular professions usually need a/an: a pilot, an artist.
Practise the sound pairs an hour / a hotel and an umbrella / a uniform.

exercises.feedback: Engineer starts with a vowel sound, and a singular job title needs an.
University begins with a consonant /y/ sound, so use a.
Young begins with a consonant sound, so use a before young dog.
Unusual starts with a vowel sound, so an is correct.

exercises.prompt: Complete with a or an: My cousin is ___ nurse at the local clinic.
exercises.feedback: Nurse begins with a consonant sound and names one profession.

exercises.prompt: Complete with a or an: We waited for ___ hour before the bus arrived.
exercises.feedback: Hour starts with a vowel sound because its h is silent.

exercises.prompt: Complete with a or an: He bought ___ useful map for the walk.
exercises.feedback: Useful starts with a consonant /y/ sound.

exercises.prompt: Complete with a or an: Could I have ___ glass of water, please?
exercises.feedback: A glass is one countable container of water.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: My brother is doctor.
exercises.feedback: The singular job title doctor needs a.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Nina found a interesting story online.
acceptedAnswers: Nina found an interesting story online.
exercises.feedback: Interesting begins with a vowel sound, so use an.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: He booked an hotel near the station.
acceptedAnswers: He booked a hotel near the station.
exercises.feedback: Hotel begins with a pronounced h consonant sound in standard modern English.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I need an uniform for my new job.
acceptedAnswers: I need a uniform for my new job.
exercises.feedback: Uniform begins with a consonant /y/ sound, so use a.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say that your sister is an architect. Begin with 'My sister'.
speakingExercises.feedback: Architect begins with a vowel sound and needs an after is.

speakingExercises.prompt: Politely request one more cup of tea. Begin with 'Could I have'.
acceptedAnswers: Could I have another cup of tea?

speakingExercises.prompt: Say that you waited for one hour. Begin with 'I waited'.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use an because hour begins with a vowel sound.

speakingExercises.prompt: You see one empty seat beside the window. Tell your friend in one sentence. Begin with 'There is' or 'There's' and include the location.
acceptedAnswers: There is an empty seat beside the window.
There's an empty seat beside the window.
speakingExercises.feedback: Empty begins with a vowel sound, so use an before empty seat. There is and there's are both natural.

speakingExercises.prompt: Change 'We saw an unusual bird.' to describe a European bird instead. Keep the subject and past tense.
speakingExercises.feedback: European starts with a consonant /y/ sound, so the article changes from an to a.

speakingExercises.prompt: You are at the information desk and need one map. Ask politely, beginning with 'Could I have' and ending with 'please'.
acceptedAnswers: Could I have a map, please?
speakingExercises.feedback: Map is a singular countable noun beginning with a consonant sound, so ask for a map.

speakingExercises.prompt: A friend says, 'It's an beautiful place.' Correct the article. Keep the rest of the sentence the same.
speakingExercises.feedback: Beautiful starts with a consonant sound, so a beautiful place is correct.

speakingExercises.prompt: At a shop, you bought one orange notebook and one yellow pencil. Tell a friend in one sentence, beginning with 'I bought' and mentioning the notebook first.
acceptedAnswers: I bought an orange notebook and a yellow pencil.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use an before the vowel sound in orange and a before the consonant sound in yellow.

listeningExercises.audioText: I picked up an umbrella because it started to rain.
listeningExercises.prompt: What did the speaker pick up?
listeningExercises.feedback: The speaker names an umbrella; an is used before its vowel sound.

listeningExercises.audioText: My aunt works as a university lecturer in Bristol.
listeningExercises.feedback: A university lecturer is the stated job; university starts with a /y/ sound.

listeningExercises.audioText: We saw an elephant beside a river.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the article spoken immediately before the animal.
listeningExercises.feedback: An is heard before elephant because elephant starts with a vowel sound.

listeningExercises.audioText: I bought an extra blanket because the nights in our cabin are very cold.
listeningExercises.prompt: Why did the speaker buy something?
choices: To carry clothes on a walk
listeningExercises.feedback: The extra blanket helps the speaker stay warm during the cold nights.

listeningExercises.audioText: My cousin is an electrician, but he works in a small bookshop on Saturdays.
listeningExercises.prompt: Where does the cousin work at weekends?
choices: At a shop that sells books
listeningExercises.feedback: The cousin works in a bookshop on Saturdays, although his profession is electrician.

listeningExercises.audioText: We have an old umbrella, but we need another one because Sam is coming too.
listeningExercises.prompt: Why is one more item needed?
choices: An additional person is joining them
They are going to throw the first item away
listeningExercises.feedback: Another means one more umbrella, needed because Sam is joining them.

listeningExercises.audioText: She found an interesting photograph in a drawer.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the article immediately before the adjective describing the photograph.
listeningExercises.feedback: You hear an before interesting, which begins with a vowel sound.

listeningExercises.audioText: Our class needs another dictionary for the new students.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the single word immediately before 'dictionary'.
listeningExercises.feedback: Another means one additional dictionary and is written as a single word.
